findings.problem: Premise 1 attributes the 12x improvement to 'the worst case (cold-fallback turns)', but the same sentence derives 12x from the 20s → 1.6s drop that it labels 'fully cached'. A cold-fallback turn is by definition a cache miss falling back to full prefill, which gets no speedup — the parenthetical contradicts the ratio it annotates.
findings.remedy: Correct the attribution: 12x is the fully-cached turn speedup (the previously worst-case ~20s turns); state separately what cold-fallback (miss) turns experience, i.e. no improvement over the uncached baseline.

findings.remedy: Fix the pointer in criterion 3 to reference the Success-criteria gating section (or add the R1-7 note to Open Questions) so a reader can find the contingency it cites.

prior.evidence: Contract rules section, Concurrency (R1-3, refined R2-1): 'single-flight on identical uncached prefixes — a concurrent request for the same prefix blocks on the in-flight prefill and is served from its result (one behavior, no either/or)' — one behavior is chosen, and Next Steps #2 requires the contract spec to include single-flight.

Approach A no longer states max_tokens: 0 as fact: it is flagged 'which must be verified against mlx-lm's server (folded into the Next Steps #3 benchmark); if rejected, fallback is max_tokens: 1 + discard the output', making warming explicitly backend-specific policy and pairing verification with a documented fallback mechanism.
